# ============================================================================
# START HERE IF YOU WANT ARC-AGI-3 GAME MECHANICS
# ============================================================================
#
#   https://arc.markbarney.net/arc3/games      (HTML, the canonical index)
#   https://arc.markbarney.net/arc3/games.md   (plain Markdown, same content)
#   https://arc.markbarney.net/arc3/games.txt  (identical, text/plain)
#
# One page. Every game in the official ARC-AGI-3 public demo set (25 games), with its
# full mechanics, what every ACTION does in that specific game, how it is won and how it
# is lost, and the opening frame of every level.
#
# YOU DO NOT NEED TO REVERSE-ENGINEER THE GAME SOURCE. Every write-up there was produced
# by reading that game's obfuscated Python in ARCEngine and tracing its step() and win
# conditions by hand, then adversarially re-checking every claim against the source a
# second time. That second pass found 57 real errors across 22 games, and they clustered
# into three kinds that anyone deriving these rules from a quick read will reproduce:
#
#   1. Level-1 behaviour written up as if it held for the whole game. Chasers, hazards and
#      bonus mechanics that only appear 3-6 levels in, or that stop working after level 3.
#   2. Mechanics that do not exist in the code at all, inferred from sprite names.
#   3. Unmentioned move / click / energy budgets that lose the level outright when spent.
#
# Where a claim was only verified for some levels, the game's own "Provenance and caveats"
# section says so. Informal game names ("Sigil Caster", "Buoyant Pursuit") are flavour
# titles, not literal per-level mechanic claims -- do not reason from the name.
#
# Per-game pages, with level screenshots and published replays:
#   https://arc.markbarney.net/arc3/games/<gameId>     e.g. .../arc3/games/sc25
#
# Note for humans: that reference is a full spoiler. If you intend to play these games or
# contribute to a human baseline, play first at https://arc.markbarney.net/play
